narrative: Material PL2__M1136593 exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.436) with a mean daily draw of 14,324 units and no detectable trend across the 169-day observation window. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.67), ranging from under 1 day to over 6 days, making them the dominant driver of safety stock requirements. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 43,401 units and a statistically derived safety stock of 25,089 units is recommended to achieve the 95% service level target while reducing total annual inventory costs by approximately 20.7% versus the current SAP configuration.
warnings: Lead time CV = 0.67 classified as unstable; occasional spikes to 6+ days inflate safety stock requirement.
SAP safety lead time of 3.0 days implies safety stock of ~42,973 units — 71% higher than statistically required.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (99.4% non-zero days) with moderate CV. The (r,Q) model is optimal for continuous-demand materials where order quantities can be fixed at the EOQ and reorder triggers are set statistically. No intermittency adjustment (Croston) is needed.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (138,514 units) is non-binding: safety_stock (25,089) + order_quantity (43,401) = 68,490 units, consuming only 49% of available capacity. No capacity-driven constraint applies.
